# Travel and Expense Policy

## Overview

This policy applies to every Larkspur Analytics employee who travels for work. Book travel through the Wayfare portal so that the finance team can see every commitment before it is paid. Trips that are booked outside the portal are reimbursed only when the traveler explains why the portal could not be used.

## Air travel

Economy class is the default for every flight. Flights longer than eight hours may be booked in premium economy without additional approval. Business class requires written approval from a vice president before the ticket is purchased. Changes to a ticket are reimbursed when the change is caused by the business purpose of the trip.

## Lodging

The nightly hotel limit is 210 US dollars in most cities and 320 US dollars in the high-cost cities listed in Appendix B. Travelers who stay with friends or family may claim a flat 40 dollar hosting allowance per night instead of a hotel rate.

## Meals

Meals are reimbursed at actual cost up to a daily limit of 75 US dollars. Alcohol is never reimbursed, even at a client dinner. Receipts are required for any single meal above 25 dollars.

## Exceptions

A manager may approve a one-time exception to the lodging limit when a conference hotel is the only reasonable option. The exception must be attached to the expense report.
documents.title: Travel and Expense Policy

documents.text:
# Expense Report Submission Guide

## Overview

Expense reports are filed in the Tally expense tool. Each report covers one trip or one calendar month of local expenses.

## Deadlines

Submit an expense report within 30 days of returning from a trip. Reports submitted after 90 days are rejected unless the finance director grants an extension. Reimbursements are paid with the next payroll cycle after the report is approved.

## Receipts

Photograph each receipt with the Tally mobile app on the day it is issued. Lost receipts can be replaced with a signed missing-receipt declaration, but no more than twice in a calendar year.

## Approval

Your direct manager approves the report first. Reports above 5,000 US dollars also need approval from the department's finance partner.
documents.title: Expense Report Submission Guide

# Hardware Refresh Program

## Overview

The hardware refresh program replaces employee laptops on a fixed cycle so that nobody works on a machine that is out of warranty. IT schedules each refresh automatically and emails the employee three weeks in advance.

## Eligibility

Engineering and data science staff receive a new laptop every three years. All other roles receive one every four years. Contractors are not eligible and use equipment supplied by their agency.

## Standard models

Engineers choose between the Corvid 16 with 64 GB of memory and the Kestrel 14 with 32 GB of memory. Other roles receive the Kestrel 14 by default. Requests for a non-standard model need a written justification from the employee's director.

## Returning old devices

The old laptop must be returned within ten business days of receiving the new one. IT wipes every returned device using a certified erasure process before it is donated or recycled.

## Exceptions

A device that fails outside warranty can be replaced early. Accidental damage is repaired first, and replaced only if the repair would cost more than half the price of a new device.
documents.title: Hardware Refresh Program

# IT Service Desk FAQ

## Overview

The service desk is open from 8:00 to 18:00 on weekdays. Urgent outages can be reported at any time through the on-call line.

## Loaner devices

Loaner laptops are available for up to two weeks while a device is being repaired. Loaners are reset to a clean image when they are returned.

## Peripherals

Every employee may order one external monitor, one keyboard and one mouse each refresh cycle. Docking stations are provided to employees who work from an office at least two days a week.

## Software requests

Software that is on the approved catalog installs automatically within an hour. Software outside the catalog goes through a security review that usually takes five business days.
documents.title: IT Service Desk FAQ

# Ledger Billing Service Runbook

## Overview

Ledger computes monthly invoices for every Larkspur customer and posts them to the payments provider. It runs as three replicas behind the internal load balancer.

## Alerts

The invoice-lag alert fires when the oldest unprocessed billing event is more than fifteen minutes old. The payment-rejection alert fires when more than two percent of posted invoices are rejected within an hour.

## First response

Acknowledge the page within five minutes. Check the Ledger dashboard for queue depth, replica health and the error rate of the payments provider. If a single replica is unhealthy, drain it and let the scheduler replace it.

## Detailed recovery procedure

When the invoice-lag alert persists after a replica has been replaced, the cause is usually a stuck batch rather than a capacity problem. Open the batch console and sort open batches by age. A batch that has been in the claimed state for more than twenty minutes without progress is considered stuck. Before you release a stuck batch, confirm that its worker is no longer running by checking the worker heartbeat table; releasing a batch whose worker is still alive produces duplicate invoices, which are expensive to reverse because the payments provider charges a fee for every refund. When the heartbeat is older than five minutes, release the batch with the release command and record the batch identifier in the incident channel. Released batches are claimed again by a healthy replica within a minute. If three or more batches are stuck at the same time, do not release them one by one; instead, pause the scheduler, because simultaneous stuck batches almost always indicate that the database connection pool is exhausted. Increase the pool only after the database team confirms there is headroom on the primary. After the scheduler is resumed, watch the invoice-lag graph for thirty minutes. The lag should fall steadily; a lag that falls and then plateaus means another batch has stuck and the procedure should be repeated from the beginning. Every release must be listed in the incident review with the time it was performed and the person who performed it, because finance reconciles each released batch against the payments provider's settlement report at the end of the month. If the settlement report shows a released batch that the payments provider never received, finance opens a reconciliation ticket and the billing team reposts that batch manually after confirming that no customer has been charged for it. Manual reposting is performed only by the billing team lead or a named deputy, never by the on-call engineer, because a repost bypasses the duplicate check that normal processing performs. The on-call engineer's responsibility ends once invoices are flowing again and every release has been recorded; the follow-up reconciliation can take several days and is tracked in the finance queue rather than in the incident channel. When the same batch becomes stuck twice in one month, the billing team opens a defect for the batch worker and attaches the heartbeat history of both incidents, so that the cause can be traced to a specific worker version. Historically, most repeated stalls were traced to long-running database transactions held open by reporting queries during month-end close, which is why reporting jobs are now scheduled outside the invoicing window on the last three days of each month.

## Escalation

Escalate to the billing team lead if invoices are not flowing again within one hour. Escalate to the finance director if any customer may have been charged twice.
documents.title: Ledger Billing Service Runbook

# On-call Handbook

## Overview

Every engineering team runs a weekly on-call rotation. The rotation hands over on Mondays at 10:00 local time.

## Expectations

The primary on-call engineer acknowledges pages within five minutes and keeps their laptop within reach. The secondary covers if the primary does not acknowledge within fifteen minutes.

## Compensation

On-call engineers receive a fixed stipend of 300 US dollars per week. A page handled between 22:00 and 07:00 also earns half a day of time off in lieu.

## Incident reviews

Every incident with customer impact gets a written review within five business days. Reviews are blameless and focus on what made the failure possible.
documents.title: On-call Handbook

# Aria-200 Sensor Datasheet

## Overview

The Aria-200 is a battery-powered environmental sensor for indoor spaces. It measures temperature, relative humidity and carbon dioxide.

## Specifications

Temperature accuracy is plus or minus 0.3 degrees Celsius. Carbon dioxide is measured with a non-dispersive infrared cell from 400 to 5,000 parts per million. The Aria-200 reports every five minutes over Bluetooth Low Energy.

## Battery

Two AA lithium cells power the Aria-200 for about eighteen months at the default reporting interval.

## Installation

Mount the sensor at head height, away from windows, doors and air vents.
documents.title: Aria-200 Sensor Datasheet

documents.text:
# Aria-300 Sensor Datasheet

## Overview

The Aria-300 extends the Aria-200 with particulate matter sensing and a LoRaWAN radio for large buildings.

## Specifications

Temperature accuracy is plus or minus 0.2 degrees Celsius. The Aria-300 also measures PM2.5 and PM10 particulates with a laser scattering sensor. It reports every minute over LoRaWAN, which reaches gateways up to two kilometers away in open space.

## Battery

The Aria-300 uses a rechargeable 6,000 mAh pack that lasts about nine months between charges at the default reporting interval.

## Installation

Mount the sensor at head height, away from windows, doors and air vents. Keep the particulate inlet free of dust covers.
documents.title: Aria-300 Sensor Datasheet

documents.text:
# Choosing an Aria Sensor

## Overview

This guide helps facilities teams choose between the Aria models.

## Recommendations

Choose the Aria-200 for offices under 2,000 square meters where a Bluetooth gateway is already installed. Choose the Aria-300 for warehouses, schools and buildings near busy roads, where particulates matter and distances are longer.

## Pricing

The Aria-200 lists at 149 US dollars per unit. The Aria-300 lists at 289 US dollars per unit, and volume discounts start at fifty units.
documents.title: Choosing an Aria Sensor

# Parental Leave Policy

## Overview

Larkspur offers paid parental leave to every employee who becomes a parent through birth, adoption or foster placement.

## Duration

Birthing parents receive twenty weeks of fully paid leave. Non-birthing parents receive sixteen weeks of fully paid leave. Leave can be taken in up to three blocks within the first year.

## Eligibility

Employees become eligible after ninety days of employment. Part-time employees receive leave in proportion to their contracted hours.

## Returning to work

Employees may return on a reduced schedule of sixty percent for the first four weeks at full pay.
documents.title: Parental Leave Policy

documents.text:
# Time Off Policy

## Overview

Time off at Larkspur is tracked in the People portal.

## Annual leave

Full-time employees accrue twenty-five days of annual leave per year. Up to five unused days carry over into the next year and expire on March 31.

## Sick leave

Sick leave is unlimited for illnesses shorter than five consecutive working days. Longer absences need a note from a medical professional.

## Public holidays

Each office observes the public holidays of its country. Employees who work on a public holiday receive a replacement day.

## Exceptions

Managers may approve unpaid leave of up to three months for personal reasons.
documents.title: Time Off Policy

documents.text:
# Data Retention Policy

## Overview

This policy sets how long Larkspur keeps customer and internal data, and how it is deleted when that period ends.

## Retention periods

Customer analytics data is kept for as long as the customer's contract is active and deleted ninety days after the contract ends. Application logs are kept for thirty days. Financial records are kept for seven years to meet tax law.

## Deletion

Deletion runs as a nightly job that removes expired records from primary storage. Backups expire on their own schedule and are fully purged within thirty-five days of the primary deletion.

## Legal holds

A legal hold suspends deletion for the data it names until the legal team releases the hold. Holds are reviewed every six months.

## Exceptions

Exceptions to a retention period require approval from the data protection officer and are recorded in the retention register.
documents.title: Data Retention Policy

documents.text:
# Customer Data Deletion Requests

## Overview

Customers can ask Larkspur to delete their data before their contract ends.

## Process

Requests are submitted through the support portal by an administrator of the customer account. Support confirms the request in writing and starts deletion within five business days.

## Timeline

Primary data is deleted within thirty days of confirmation. The customer receives a deletion certificate once backups have also been purged.

## Limits

Invoices and payment records are excluded from deletion requests because they are financial records.
documents.title: Customer Data Deletion Requests

# Harbor Point Office Move

## Overview

The Portland team moves from the Alder Street office to the new Harbor Point building in the autumn.

## Timeline

Packing crates are delivered on October 6. The final working day at Alder Street is October 17, and Harbor Point opens on October 20. Everyone works from home on October 18 and 19 while movers relocate equipment.

## What to pack

Pack personal items and paper files in the labeled crates. IT moves monitors, docks and desk phones; do not pack them yourself.

## Parking

Harbor Point has eighty parking spaces, allocated by a quarterly lottery. Bicycle storage has room for sixty bicycles and includes showers.
documents.title: Harbor Point Office Move

documents.text:
# Harbor Point Building Guide

## Overview

Harbor Point is a five-story building on the riverfront. Larkspur occupies the third and fourth floors.

## Access

Badges issued for Alder Street work at Harbor Point after October 20. Visitors check in at the ground floor reception, which is staffed from 7:30 to 18:30.

## Meeting rooms

The fourth floor has twelve meeting rooms, including two rooms for twenty people. Rooms are booked in the calendar like any other resource.

## Kitchen

Each floor has a kitchen. Coffee and fruit are provided; lunch is catered on Wednesdays.
documents.title: Harbor Point Building Guide

# Q3 Customer Research Findings

## Overview

The research team interviewed twenty-four customers between July and September about how they use Larkspur dashboards.

## Key findings

Eighteen of the twenty-four customers export dashboards to spreadsheets at least weekly, mostly to combine Larkspur data with their own budget figures. Customers in healthcare asked repeatedly for audit trails that show who viewed a dashboard. Only three customers used the alerting feature, and most did not know it existed.

## Pain points

The most common complaint was slow loading of dashboards with more than twenty charts. Several customers described the sharing dialog as confusing because it mixes viewers and editors in one list.

## Recommendations

The team recommends a native spreadsheet connector, a viewer audit log for regulated customers, and an onboarding tour that introduces alerting.
documents.title: Q3 Customer Research Findings

documents.text:
# Research Method Notes

## Overview

These notes describe how the Q3 interviews were conducted.

## Recruitment

Participants were recruited from active accounts with at least ten weekly users. Each participant received a 100 US dollar gift card.

## Sessions

Each interview lasted forty-five minutes and was recorded with consent. Two researchers attended every session, one leading and one taking notes.

## Analysis

Notes were coded independently by both researchers, and disagreements were resolved in a joint session.
documents.title: Research Method Notes

# Larkspur Data API Reference

## Overview

The Larkspur Data API gives programmatic access to dashboards, datasets and query results. All endpoints use HTTPS and JSON.

## Authentication

Requests authenticate with a bearer token created in the account settings. Tokens expire after ninety days and can be revoked at any time.

## Rate limits

Standard accounts may send 600 requests per minute. Enterprise accounts may send 3,000 requests per minute. A request over the limit receives HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header in seconds.

## Pagination

List endpoints return at most 200 items per page and include a cursor for the next page.

## Versioning and deprecation

The API is versioned in the URL path, for example /v3/datasets. A version is supported for at least eighteen months after its successor is released. When a version is deprecated, every response from it carries a Deprecation header with the retirement date, and account administrators receive an email ninety days before retirement and again thirty days before retirement. Breaking changes are only ever introduced in a new version; within a version, Larkspur may add optional fields to responses and new optional parameters to requests, so clients must ignore fields they do not recognise. Error responses always contain a machine-readable code and a human-readable message, and the codes listed in the error catalogue never change meaning within a version. Clients that need longer to migrate can request an extension of up to six months through their account manager, which is granted for enterprise accounts that have a written migration plan. During an extension the retired version keeps working for that account only and is excluded from the standard availability commitment, so incidents affecting it are handled on a best-effort basis. Version three is the current version; version two was deprecated in January and retires at the end of July. After retirement, requests to a retired version receive HTTP 410 Gone with a link to the migration guide, and no data is returned. The migration guide lists every field that was renamed or removed between versions, together with the replacement field where one exists. Most clients need to change three things when moving from version two to version three: dataset identifiers are now strings rather than integers, timestamps are returned in UTC with an explicit offset, and list endpoints use cursor pagination instead of page numbers. The Python and JavaScript client libraries handle all three changes automatically from release 4.0 onwards, so clients that use a current library usually only need to upgrade the library and run their tests. Clients that call the API directly should test against the sandbox environment, which mirrors production data structures with synthetic data and is reset every Sunday. Larkspur support can review a migration plan on request, and enterprise customers can schedule a call with an API engineer to discuss unusual integrations. Usage of each version is shown in the account's API dashboard, which helps administrators find forgotten scripts that still call an old version before it retires.
documents.title: Larkspur Data API Reference

# API Quickstart

## Overview

This quickstart shows how to run a first query with the Larkspur Data API.

## Create a token

Open account settings, choose API tokens and create a token with read access to the datasets you need.

## Run a query

Send a POST request to /v3/queries with the dataset identifier and a SQL statement. Queries that take longer than thirty seconds return a job identifier that you can poll.

## Next steps

Use the Python client library to handle pagination and retries automatically.
documents.title: API Quickstart

# Fenwick Lab Chemical Storage Rules

## Overview

These rules apply to every person who stores or handles chemicals in the Fenwick sensor calibration lab.

## Storage

Flammable solvents are stored in the yellow cabinet and never above eye level. Acids and bases are stored in separate ventilated cabinets. Every container carries a label with its contents, owner and date of opening.

## Quantities

No more than ten liters of flammable solvent may be kept in the lab at any time. Larger deliveries go to the central store.

## Spills

Small spills under one liter are cleaned with the spill kit by the person who caused them. Larger spills require evacuating the room and calling the site safety officer.

## Exceptions

Exceptions are approved by the site safety officer and posted on the lab door.
documents.title: Fenwick Lab Chemical Storage Rules

documents.text:
# Fenwick Lab Access and Training

## Overview

The Fenwick lab is a restricted area.

## Training

New users complete a two-hour safety course and a supervised session before they receive badge access. Training is refreshed every year.

## Working alone

Nobody may handle chemicals alone in the lab after 19:00. Calibration work without chemicals can be done alone if the user checks in with security.

## Protective equipment

Safety glasses are required at all times. Nitrile gloves and a lab coat are required when handling any chemical.
documents.title: Fenwick Lab Access and Training

documents.text:
# Community Partner Grant Program

## Overview

The Larkspur community grant funds nonprofit organizations that use data to improve public services in the cities where Larkspur has offices.

## Funding

The program awards up to twelve grants a year. Each grant is between 10,000 and 40,000 US dollars and covers one year of work. Grantees also receive a free Team plan for the grant period.

## Eligibility

Applicants must be registered nonprofits with an annual budget under two million US dollars. Political campaigns and individual researchers are not eligible.

## Timeline

Applications open on February 1 and close on March 15. Finalists are interviewed in April, and awards are announced on May 20.

## Reporting

Grantees submit a short progress report after six months and a final report with outcomes at the end of the year.
documents.title: Community Partner Grant Program

documents.text:
# Grant Review Guidelines

## Overview

These guidelines tell reviewers how to score grant applications.

## Scoring

Each application is scored by three reviewers on impact, feasibility and use of data, each from one to five. Impact counts double in the total score.

## Conflicts of interest

Reviewers declare any relationship with an applicant and do not score that application.

## Decisions

The grant committee selects finalists from the twenty highest total scores and makes the final decision after interviews.
documents.title: Grant Review Guidelines

documents.text:
# Engineering Onboarding Checklist

## Overview

This checklist covers an engineer's first two weeks at Larkspur.

## First day

Collect your laptop and badge from IT, set up multi-factor authentication and join the engineering chat channels. Your buddy meets you for lunch.

## First week

Clone the main repositories and run the local development environment. Complete the security awareness course by Friday. Ship one small change, such as a documentation fix, through code review.

## Second week

Shadow the on-call engineer for at least one shift. Meet your manager to agree on goals for the first ninety days.

## Exceptions

Engineers who join in December complete the security course in their first week back after the holidays.
documents.title: Engineering Onboarding Checklist

documents.text:
# Onboarding Buddy Guide

## Overview

Every new engineer is paired with a buddy from a neighboring team for their first month.

## Responsibilities

The buddy answers everyday questions, reviews the newcomer's first pull request and introduces them to at least five colleagues.

## Time commitment

Buddies should expect to spend about three hours a week on the role in the first two weeks, and one hour a week after that.

## Recognition

Buddying counts toward the mentoring expectation in the engineering career framework.
documents.title: Onboarding Buddy Guide

# Postmortem: March Queue Outage

## Summary

On March 12, the ingestion queue stopped delivering events for two hours and forty minutes. Dashboards showed stale data for every customer during that time, but no data was lost.

## Impact

Roughly 1,900 customer accounts saw dashboards that were up to three hours old. Forty-one support tickets were opened.

## Timeline and root cause

At 09:05 UTC a routine certificate rotation replaced the certificate used by the queue brokers. The new certificate had been issued for the wrong internal hostname, so every consumer that reconnected after the rotation failed its TLS handshake and backed off. Because consumers reconnect gradually as their connections age, the failure did not appear all at once; delivery fell to half its normal rate at 09:40 and stopped completely at 10:20. The queue-depth alert fired at 10:25, but the on-call engineer first investigated the brokers' disk usage, which was also high because undelivered events were accumulating. At 11:05 a second engineer noticed TLS errors in the consumer logs. The previous certificate was restored at 11:30, and consumers recovered within ten minutes. The backlog of roughly forty million events was fully processed by 13:00. The certificate was wrong because the rotation tool selected a template by prefix, and a new template with a similar name had been added the week before. Nothing in the rotation process checked that the certificate matched the hostnames that clients actually use, and the staging queue, where the same rotation had run a day earlier, uses a different hostname scheme that happened to match the wrong template. During the outage, the support team posted a status page update at 10:50, thirty minutes after delivery stopped completely, and updated it every half hour until recovery. Customers who opened tickets were told that their data was delayed rather than lost, which the team could say confidently because the queue retains events for seventy-two hours. After recovery, the processing pipeline worked through the backlog at roughly three times its normal rate, which briefly raised database load on the processing side; no further alerts fired during the catch-up period. The incident commander declared the incident resolved at 13:10, once the backlog had been processed and dashboards for a sample of customers were confirmed to be current. A follow-up review found that the rotation tool's logs had recorded the template it selected, but nobody reviewed those logs as part of the rotation, and the tool reported success because the installation itself completed without error. The team also found that the queue-depth alert threshold had been set high to avoid noise during normal traffic peaks, which delayed detection by several minutes; the threshold is being revisited separately from the action items below.

## Action items

Add a hostname check to the rotation tool before any certificate is installed. Alert on consumer TLS handshake failures directly. Make the staging queue use the production hostname scheme.
documents.title: Postmortem: March Queue Outage

# Ingestion Queue Overview

## Overview

The ingestion queue carries raw events from customer integrations to the processing pipeline.

## Capacity

The queue runs on six brokers and handles about ninety thousand events per second at peak.

## Retention

Events are retained for seventy-two hours, which is why a delivery outage shorter than three days does not lose data.

## Ownership

The data platform team owns the queue and its on-call rotation.
documents.title: Ingestion Queue Overview

documents.text:
# Vendor Approval Process

## Overview

Every new supplier of software or services must be approved before Larkspur signs a contract or pays an invoice.

## Steps

The requester submits a vendor request in the procurement portal with the business purpose and expected annual spend. Procurement checks the vendor's financial standing. If the vendor will process customer data, the security team completes a risk assessment.

## Thresholds

Purchases under 5,000 US dollars a year need only the requester's manager. Purchases between 5,000 and 50,000 dollars also need the department head. Anything above 50,000 dollars goes to the chief financial officer.

## Timelines

A standard approval takes about ten business days. A security risk assessment adds up to fifteen business days.

## Exceptions

Emergency purchases may proceed with the CFO's verbal approval, followed by a vendor request within five business days.
documents.title: Vendor Approval Process

documents.text:
# Approved Vendor List

## Overview

The approved vendor list names suppliers that have already passed review.

## Using the list

Teams can buy from an approved vendor without repeating the security assessment, as long as the new purchase does not change the kind of data the vendor handles.

## Renewal

Every approved vendor is reviewed again every two years, or sooner if its ownership changes.

## Removal

Vendors are removed from the list after a security incident until a new assessment is completed.
documents.title: Approved Vendor List

documents.text:
# Sustainability Report: Data Center Energy

## Overview

This report covers the electricity used by Larkspur's two data center regions over the last calendar year.

## Consumption

The Oregon region used 4.1 gigawatt-hours, and the Frankfurt region used 2.6 gigawatt-hours. Average power usage effectiveness was 1.18 in Oregon and 1.31 in Frankfurt.

## Renewable share

Oregon was supplied entirely by hydroelectric and wind power through a power purchase agreement. Frankfurt reached sixty-two percent renewable supply through certificates.

## Targets

Larkspur aims for one hundred percent renewable supply in every region by the end of next year and a power usage effectiveness below 1.25 everywhere.
documents.title: Sustainability Report: Data Center Energy

documents.text:
# Hardware Efficiency Program

## Overview

The efficiency program reduces the energy used per customer query.

## Measures

Storage servers older than five years are replaced with denser models that use about forty percent less power per terabyte. Idle compute capacity is powered down overnight in both regions.

## Results so far

Energy per thousand queries fell by eighteen percent compared with the previous year.
documents.title: Hardware Efficiency Program

documents.text:
# Access Review Standard

## Overview

Access reviews confirm that every person still needs the system access they hold.

## Frequency

Production systems are reviewed every quarter. Internal tools are reviewed twice a year. Access for people who leave Larkspur is removed within four hours of their departure.

## Reviewers

The owner of each system reviews its access list and must confirm or remove every entry. Owners cannot approve their own access.

## Evidence

Each review is exported from the identity provider and kept for three years for audits.

## Exceptions

Emergency access is granted for at most twenty-four hours and is reviewed the next business day.
documents.title: Access Review Standard

documents.text:
# Multi-factor Authentication Guide

## Overview

Every Larkspur account must use multi-factor authentication.

## Approved methods

Hardware security keys are the preferred method and are required for administrators. Authenticator apps are allowed for everyone else. Text-message codes are not accepted.

## Lost keys

Report a lost security key to IT immediately. IT disables the key and issues a temporary authenticator enrollment valid for seven days.

## Exceptions

There are no exceptions to multi-factor authentication for any employee or contractor.
documents.title: Multi-factor Authentication Guide

documents.text:
# Board Meeting Minutes, May

## Attendance

All seven directors attended. The chief executive and chief financial officer presented.

## Financial update

Revenue for the first quarter was 18.4 million US dollars, nine percent above plan. Operating costs were two percent above plan because of hiring in engineering.

## Decisions

The board approved opening a sales office in Singapore in the fourth quarter. The board deferred a decision on acquiring the data visualization startup Quill until the August meeting, pending further due diligence.

## Risks discussed

Directors asked for a plan to reduce dependence on the three largest customers, who together account for twenty-two percent of revenue.

## Next meeting

The next meeting is scheduled for August 14.
documents.title: Board Meeting Minutes, May

documents.text:
# Board Meeting Minutes, February

## Attendance

Six of seven directors attended.

## Financial update

Revenue for the previous year was 64 million US dollars, four percent below plan.

## Decisions

The board approved the annual budget with a hiring plan of sixty new roles. The board asked management to evaluate expansion into Southeast Asia and report back in May.

## Next meeting

The next meeting is scheduled for May 9.
documents.title: Board Meeting Minutes, February

documents.text:
# Pricing Plans

## Overview

Larkspur sells three plans: Starter, Team and Enterprise. Prices are per month and billed annually.

## Starter

Starter costs 49 US dollars for up to three users and ten dashboards. Data is refreshed every twenty-four hours.

## Team

Team costs 25 US dollars per user with a minimum of five users. It includes unlimited dashboards and hourly data refresh.

## Enterprise

Enterprise pricing is quoted per contract. It adds single sign-on, a viewer audit log, a dedicated account manager and refresh every five minutes.

## Overview of support

Starter includes email support. Team adds chat support during business hours. Enterprise includes a four-hour response commitment around the clock.
documents.title: Pricing Plans

documents.text:
# Discounts and Billing

## Overview

This page describes discounts and billing terms for all plans.

## Discounts

Registered nonprofits receive forty percent off Team and Enterprise. Education customers receive fifty percent off Team.

## Billing

Plans are billed annually in advance. Monthly billing is available for Team at a fifteen percent premium.

## Cancellation

Annual plans can be cancelled at any time, with a refund for unused full months.
documents.title: Discounts and Billing

documents.text:
# Internship Hiring Process

## Overview

Larkspur hires summer interns in engineering, data science and design.

## Timeline

Applications open in September and close on November 30. Interviews run from December to February, and offers are sent by March 1.

## Interviews

Candidates complete one forty-five-minute technical interview and one thirty-minute conversation with a future team member. There is no take-home assignment.

## Compensation

Interns are paid a monthly stipend of 5,200 US dollars. Interns who relocate receive a one-time housing allowance of 2,000 dollars.

## Return offers

Interns who meet their goals receive a return offer for a full-time role or a second internship.
documents.title: Internship Hiring Process

documents.text:
# Intern Program Handbook

## Overview

The intern program runs for twelve weeks between June and August.

## Mentors

Each intern has a mentor who meets them at least twice a week and a manager who sets their project goals.

## Final presentations

Interns present their project to the company in the last week of the program.

## Housing

Larkspur does not arrange housing but shares a list of short-term rentals near each office.

# Irrigation Sensor Field Trial Report

## Overview

Larkspur trialled soil moisture sensors at three farms for one growing season to test whether sensor-guided irrigation saves water without reducing yield.

## Sites

The trial ran at Millbrook Orchard (apples), Dunmore Fields (sweetcorn) and Ash Hollow Vineyard (grapes). Each site split its land into a sensor-guided half and a half irrigated on the farm's usual schedule.

## Results by site

At Millbrook Orchard, the sensor-guided half used twenty-seven percent less water than the scheduled half, and apple yield was unchanged within the margin of measurement error. The orchard manager noted that the sensors recommended skipping irrigation on several cool days in early summer when the usual schedule would have watered, and those skipped days accounted for most of the saving. At Dunmore Fields the saving was smaller, at eleven percent, because sweetcorn needs heavy watering during tasseling, and the sensors agreed with the schedule during that period; outside tasseling, the savings were similar to the orchard's. Sweetcorn yield was two percent higher on the sensor-guided half, but the difference is within the variation normally seen between fields. At Ash Hollow Vineyard, the sensor-guided half used thirty-four percent less water, the largest saving in the trial, but grape yield fell by six percent. The vineyard manager considered the lower yield acceptable because the grapes had a higher sugar content, which is valued for winemaking; however, the trial was not designed to measure grape quality, so this observation is anecdotal. Across all three sites, sensor faults were rare: four of the ninety deployed sensors failed during the season, all because of rodent damage to cables, and each failed sensor was replaced within two days. Installation took one day per site, using a crew of two technicians, and calibration against hand-held reference readings was repeated after the first month at every site. The gateways at all three sites ran on solar power without interruption, although the vineyard gateway had to be moved once because vines shaded its panel in midsummer. Data from the sensors reached the Larkspur dashboard with a median delay of four minutes, which farm managers considered more than sufficient for irrigation decisions made once or twice a day. Farm managers at all three sites reported that the dashboard's daily recommendation was easy to follow, but two of them asked for a weekly summary that compares water use with the previous season. The orchard manager also asked for an alert when soil moisture falls below a set level overnight, because irrigation at the orchard is often started early in the morning before staff check the dashboard. Weather during the season was close to the ten-year average, with a slightly wetter June than usual, so the results may overstate savings in a dry year; the report recommends repeating the trial over at least two further seasons before drawing firm conclusions.

## Conclusions

Sensor-guided irrigation saved water at every site. Yield was unaffected for apples and sweetcorn. The effect on grapes needs a dedicated trial that measures quality as well as yield.

# Field Trial Plan

## Overview

This plan was written before the irrigation trial started.

## Hypothesis

Sensor-guided irrigation reduces water use by at least fifteen percent with no loss of yield.

## Equipment

Each site receives thirty soil moisture sensors and one solar-powered gateway.

## Budget

The trial budget is 86,000 US dollars, including sensors, installation and two site visits per farm.
